Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

you pronoun

more than one

also you all, you two, you guys, ye, with you

classical

Ter. Ph. 478: omnēs vōs amō
Liv. 1.56.10: quī vestrum prīmus … ōsculum mātrī tulerit

vōs, vestrum (vestrī)

pronoun, second person plural: dative and ablative vōbīs

you (more than one)

Said only to more than one person. Left out like tū unless stressed. Of the two genitives, vestrum means “of you” as a part of the group (quis vestrum, which of you; ūnusquisque vestrum), vestrī is the object of a feeling or a thought (memor vestrī, mindful of you). “With you” is vōbīscum.

Examples

  • Mī Geta, omnēs vōs amō.

    My dear Geta, I love you all.Ter. Ph. 478

  • quid vōs, adhūc nōn cēnāstis?

    What, you haven’t had dinner yet?Petr. 74.2

  • vōs hīc hodiē cēnātōte ambō. — Fīat. — Plausum date.

    You two will dine here tonight, both of you. — So be it. — Give us your applause.Plaut. Rud. 1423–1423c

  • imperium summum Rōmae habēbit quī vestrum prīmus, ō juvenēs, ōsculum mātrī tulerit

    Whichever of you, young men, is the first to kiss his mother shall hold the highest power at Rome.Liv. 1.56.10

  • vōs, meae cārissimae animae, quam saepissimē ad mē scrībite et vōs quid agātis et quid istīc agātur

    You, my dearest souls, write to me as often as you can, both how you are and what is going on there.Cic. Fam. 14.14.2

  • Bene ambulētis, et sit Deus in itinere vestrō, et angelus ejus comitētur vōbīscum.

    Have a good journey; God be on your way, and his angel go with you.Vulg. Tob. 5.21

See also you, your, yourselves, we.
